stem: An uninsured adult arrives at a Medicare-participating hospital emergency department reporting severe chest pain. Registration staff ask whether payment can be arranged before the client is evaluated. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Ensure the client receives an appropriate medical screening examination without delaying it for payment or insurance issues, and proceed with stabilization or appropriate transfer if an emergency medical condition is identified
options.B: Delay the medical screening examination until the client provides proof of insurance or pays a deposit
options.C: Direct the client to an outpatient clinic solely because the client is uninsured, without an emergency medical screening examination
options.D: Explain that EMTALA protections apply only to Medicare beneficiaries rather than to all individuals who present for emergency evaluation

rationale: EMTALA requires Medicare-participating hospitals with emergency services to provide an appropriate medical screening examination when an individual presents requesting examination or treatment for a possible emergency medical condition, regardless of insurance status or ability to pay. If an emergency medical condition exists, the hospital must provide stabilizing treatment within its capability or an appropriate transfer. Insurance questions may be asked only if they do not delay examination or treatment.
educational_objective: Protect emergency-care access by applying EMTALA requirements for medical screening, stabilization, and non-delayed care regardless of ability to pay.
source_document_title: Emergency Medical Treatment & Labor Act (EMTALA); You have rights in an emergency room under EMTALA

audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; possible EMC requires screening before disposition based on ability to pay.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; protections are not limited to Medicare beneficiaries.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A complies with current EMTALA requirements.
